Section 4 • \(\xi\)3D

4.8 Particularization for \(L=2, 3\) and subset-pair representations

Particularizing Eq. (4.16) for \(L=2 \longrightarrow \mathcal{C} = C_{12}\) we can regroup terms to obtain: \begin{align} &\xi\!\left(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta\right) \;\equiv\; \Big\langle \delta^{(s)}\left(\Lambda_\alpha\right)\, \delta^{(s)}(\Lambda_\beta) \Big\rangle_{\rm ens} \;=\; \int_{\Omega}\! d\mathbb P(\omega)\; \delta\left(\Lambda_\alpha,\omega\right)\, \delta\left(\Lambda_\beta,\omega\right) \; = \notag \\ &= \frac{1}{ \bigl[1+\TextZero{C_{12}(\Lambda_\alpha)}\bigr] \bigl[1+\TextZero{C_{12}(\Lambda_\beta)}\bigr] } \Bigg[ - \TextZero{C_{12}(\Lambda_\alpha)\,C_{12}(\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextTwo{\xi_{11}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextTwo{\xi_{22}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextTwo{\xi_{12,\mathrm{sym}}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \notag\\[0.6em] &\qquad + \TextThree{\xi_{1(12), \mathrm{sym}}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextThree{\xi_{2(12), \mathrm{sym}}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} + \TextFour{\xi_{(12)(12)}(\Lambda_\alpha,\Lambda_\beta)} \Bigg]. \tag{4.20} \end{align}

Conceptually, the same result for Eq. (4.20) can be obtained by using Table 1:

Just for illustrative purposes, we can also obtain the analogous expression for the \(L=3\) case using Table 2, which is more complex but follows the same principles:

FROM ANDREU’s notes From now on, for simplicity, we ignore the redshift evolution of the mean fluxes, and look at the fluctuations in two pixels:

\begin{align} \xi_T(\Delta \theta, \Delta) & = \left< \delta_T(\hat n_1, \Lambda_\alpha) ~ \delta_T(\hat n_2, \Lambda_\beta) \right> \nonumber \\ & = \left( 1 + C_{12} \right)^{-2} \left[ 1 + 2 C_{12} + \xi_\alpha (\Delta \theta, \Delta) + \xi_X (\Delta \theta, \Delta) + \xi_{\alpha X} (\Delta \theta, \Delta) \right. \nonumber \\ & \left. \qquad + C^2_{\alpha X} + \xi_3 (\Delta \theta, \Delta) \right] - 1 ~, \tag{4.21} \end{align}
